reference.title: Smith Decline Bench Press
reference.listing: Video (title from the listing URL; the page could not be fetched from this environment, so the movement follows the exercise name and standard coaching)
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

breathing.pattern: Breathe in and brace as you lower the bar, hold it through the touch, breathe out as you press it up.
breathing.cadence: About 2.0 s down, 0.3 s touch, 1.2 s up

prescription.tempo: 2-0-1-0 (2 s down, no pause, 1 s up)
prescription.load: Barbell load is user-chosen: pick a weight you can press for the target reps with 1-3 reps in reserve (RIR 1-3, about RPE 7-9).
prescription.progression: Add reps up to the top of the range, then add 1.25-2.5 kg.

cues.text: Lie on a decline bench under the Smith bar, head at the low end, knees bent over the top and feet hooked under the roller; shoulder blades back and down. Grip overhand about 1.5 times shoulder width, turn the bar off the pegs and hold it up with straight arms.
Breathe in and lower the bar straight down the rails to the lower chest, elbows about 45-60 degrees from the body.
Touch the lower chest lightly, no bounce; shoulder blades stay pinned, glutes stay on the bench.
Breathe out and press straight back up the rails to straight arms.
Arms straight, re-brace and go again; after the last rep turn the bar back onto the pegs.

mistakes.mistake: Elbows flared straight out at 90 degrees (a "T")
mistakes.fix: Tuck the elbows to about 45-60 degrees so the bar lands on the lower chest.

mistakes.mistake: Bouncing the bar off the chest
mistakes.fix: Lower under control and touch lightly before pressing.
Keep the glutes on the bench and drive through the feet; a slight arch in the upper back is fine, a bridge is not.

mistakes.mistake: Wrists bent back under the bar
mistakes.fix: Stack the bar over the heel of the palm, wrist and forearm.
Grip evenly using the bar markings and press both hands at the same speed; lighten the load.

kinematics.norm: Decline of about 15-30 degrees, head low; the lower (sternocostal) pectoralis is emphasised in decline pressing (common coaching)
kinematics.setup: 20° decline, head at the low end
kinematics.peak: Upper back and head on the board (rig shapes)

kinematics.norm: About 1.5 times shoulder width is a common middle grip (Saeterbakken 2021)
kinematics.setup: 78 cm between the bar grips (≈2.0x the shoulder-joint width)

kinematics.norm: Arms straight but not locked at the top; deeply bent with the bar on the chest (clinical opinion)
kinematics.peak: ≈118° with the bar on the chest

kinematics.measure: Elbow flare (upper arm from the trunk)
kinematics.norm: About 45-60 degrees from the body at the bottom (clinical opinion)
kinematics.setup: Arms reaching up to the bar
kinematics.peak: ≈55° from the trunk at the bottom

kinematics.norm: Fixed by the vertical rails: straight down to the lower chest and straight back up (common coaching)
kinematics.setup: Vertical rails through the lower chest; top 102.5 cm high
kinematics.peak: Bar on the chest at 71.4 cm; 31.1 cm of travel

kinematics.norm: Knees bent over the end of the bench, feet hooked under the roller (machine design)
Controlled: about 2 s down and 1-2 s up (clinical opinion)
kinematics.peak: 2 s down, 0.3 s touch, 1.2 s up

Saeterbakken, van den Tillaar and Fimland 2011, a comparison of muscle activity and 1-RM strength of three chest-press exercises with different stability requirements (J Sports Sci 29(5):533-538; PubMed 21225489)

Saeterbakken, Stien, Pedersen, Solstad, Cumming and Andersen 2021, the effect of grip width on muscle strength and electromyographic activity in bench press among novice- and resistance-trained men (Int J Environ Res Public Health 18(12):6444; PMC8296276)

cautions: Set the safety stops just under the lowest bar position before the first rep; the bar cannot go lower than them.
Practise turning the bar on and off the pegs (a small turn of the wrists) with an empty bar first.
The rails fix the bar path: place yourself so the movement feels natural for the joints, and do not force range.
Hook the feet under the roller before lying back, and sit up only after the bar is back on the pegs.
The head-down position raises pressure in the head: keep sets short and sit up slowly.
Stop if sharp pain, numbness or tingling occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Shoulder discomfort: a slightly narrower grip with the elbows tucked a little more, or a dumbbell press.
Lower back arching too much: feet on a low step or on the end of the bench.
regressions: Floor press (the floor limits the depth).
progressions: Pause bench press (1-2 s on the chest).
Close-grip bench press for the triceps.

muscleNotes.pec_r: Main pusher: horizontal adduction and flexion of the upper arm. On a flat bench the middle (sternal) and lower (costal) fibres were most active (Rodríguez-Ridao 2020), and pectoralis activity was similar for barbell, dumbbell and Smith machine presses (Saeterbakken 2011).
muscleNotes.pec_l: Main pusher: horizontal adduction and flexion of the upper arm. On a flat bench the middle (sternal) and lower (costal) fibres were most active (Rodríguez-Ridao 2020), and pectoralis activity was similar for barbell, dumbbell and Smith machine presses (Saeterbakken 2011).
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Flexes the shoulder with the chest; its activity was similar across barbell and dumbbell presses (Saeterbakken 2011).
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_l: Flexes the shoulder with the chest; its activity was similar across barbell and dumbbell presses (Saeterbakken 2011).
muscleNotes.triceps_r: Straightens the elbows in the top half; triceps activity was higher with a barbell than with dumbbells (Saeterbakken 2011).
muscleNotes.triceps_l: Straightens the elbows in the top half; triceps activity was higher with a barbell than with dumbbells (Saeterbakken 2011).
muscleNotes.serratus_r: Holds the shoulder blades against the rib cage as the bar is pressed.
muscleNotes.serratus_l: Holds the shoulder blades against the rib cage as the bar is pressed.
muscleNotes.biceps_r: A minor stabiliser; less active with the fixed barbell than with dumbbells (Saeterbakken 2011).
muscleNotes.biceps_l: A minor stabiliser; less active with the fixed barbell than with dumbbells (Saeterbakken 2011).
muscleNotes.infraspinatus_r: Rotator cuff: centres the head of the upper arm in the socket (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.infraspinatus_l: Rotator cuff: centres the head of the upper arm in the socket (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_r: Keep the shoulder blades pinned back and down on the bench.
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_l: Keep the shoulder blades pinned back and down on the bench.
muscleNotes.lats_r: Help control the bar on the way down and keep the upper back tight.
muscleNotes.lats_l: Help control the bar on the way down and keep the upper back tight.
muscleNotes.core: Bracing keeps the ribs down and the pelvis on the bench.

phases.label: Arms straight, bar over the shoulders

guides.label: Press up and slightly back over the shoulders
Elbows bent to bring the bar to the chest
